authoritative_inventory.source: Authenticated Vercel REST: project, all deployment pages, aliases, exact deployment details and firewall active/draft listing

corrections: Release validates and allows both App public aliases instead of accidentally denying the real public URL
Primary and fallback artifacts require Production configuration, in addition to project, READY, exact SHA and hostname checks
API Preview hop requires explicit --preview-deployment at the same SHA, Preview target, V2 branch and deployed isolation environment keys
The fixed Preview alias must point to that explicit Preview artifact
Public aliases may resolve only to selected Production artifacts, never to the Preview artifact
All verified hostnames are deduplicated and sorted before plan digest and rule generation

validation.live_app_release_dry_run: passed with both actual public aliases

execution_limits: No firewall rule was staged or activated; this is readiness evidence, not a live denial proof
Vercel deployment details expose environment key names, not their values: namespace=preview and the actual QA recipient allowlist must be verified from deployment creation/runtime evidence separately
The current Production API and Preview use different SHAs; the guard will refuse to combine them as a final compatible release selection
The real App public alias is not listed among the project's current domains, so promotion alone must not be assumed to move it; confirm or assign both aliases before release mode

After controlled activation, prove old authenticated immutable/branch hosts cannot reach runtime, verify both public App aliases and the exact Preview hop, and test old deployment pinning parameters/headers
Anonymous Deployment Protection redirects are not themselves evidence of WAF denial
